## Trial `internal-time-sync-rhel10__pUqg4eJ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 was configured to serve time (allow rule, firewall opened, listening on port 123, and directly shown serving node2 as a client both before and after node1's own reboot), and node2 was reconfigured to sync exclusively from node1 (public pool directive removed, `server 10.100.93.10 iburst prefer` added, and chronyc sources/tracking directly showing node1 selected as the sole source, verified again after node2's reboot). The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed cleanly on both nodes with full pre/ack/post-boot-id/recovery evidence consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is high; the only minor issue is unremoved diagnostic scratch files left in /tmp on both nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 33/6 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **node1-internal-time-source — Satisfied:** node1 configured as the internal time source for the cluster (serves NTP to node2)
  - **Why:** node1's /etc/chrony.conf was updated with `allow 10.100.93.11/32` and `local stratum 10`, chronyd was restarted and confirmed active, firewalld opened the ntp service, and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot shows chronyd listening on 0.0.0.0:123 (server mode) in addition to the client-only 127.0.0.1:323/[::1]:323 sockets seen pre-change. `chronyc clients` on node1 directly shows node2 (vm-rhel7-4277807675) polling as an active NTP client, both immediately after configuration and again after node1's own reboot, confirming the server role persisted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-6d675b566a984865`, `cmd-7dfef2bab4d3495c`, `cmd-17270bf4ed024e6a`, `cmd-1b36ae9eda7c4318`, `cmd-ed14488eb3a94484`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`, `global:before_prepare:node1:listening-sockets`
- **node2-sync-from-node1 — Satisfied:** node2 configured to synchronize its clock against node1 instead of a public time server
  - **Why:** node2's /etc/chrony.conf had the `pool 2.rhel.pool.ntp.org iburst` directive removed and replaced with `server 10.100.93.10 iburst prefer` (node1's IP). After restarting chronyd, `chronyc -n sources` and `chronyc tracking` on node2 show `^* 10.100.93.10` as the sole/selected source (Reference ID 0A645D0A), with no public servers present. This relationship was re-verified after node2's own reboot as well.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-37dee552e20b4809`, `cmd-37242a0f46df4592`, `cmd-e77bfe15058b49f8`, `cmd-b80e9b41433442e1`, `cmd-74f55eddf8504bf3`, `cmd-864d2a03218d47d7`
- **provider-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** (Independent of task contract) provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/cluster state
  - **Why:** Both nodes show a complete before/ack/after transition: pre-restart boot_id and healthy chrony state captured (cmd-a36511fc2af244f6, cmd-e3fcdb50ecb84385), `systemctl reboot` acknowledged before disconnect with subsequent connection timeouts confirming downtime (cmd-64b0796c9dd54eaa..cmd-5997501e43d04c64 for node1; cmd-643e537e443b4e63..cmd-5e8f1466e1304fd1 for node2), changed boot_id post-restart matching the fixed after-executor snapshot (cmd-c7eb685a3d894bca / global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity; cmd-5ebde53801bf4817 / global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity), and recovered chronyd + persisted config + restored sync relationship on both nodes (cmd-f8b4e8fa3ead4522, cmd-9dc7ef8c420e4a4c, cmd-88ba5f3c874c4ed2, cmd-d82227a4f4dd4990 for node1; cmd-2a3bf1a890d04123, cmd-864d2a03218d47d7, cmd-ed14488eb3a94484 for node2).

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Executor commands were almost entirely read-only diagnostics or directly purposeful configuration changes (chrony.conf edits, chronyd restarts, firewall rule, reboots) with clear ties to the task or the restart protocol. The only unnecessary residue is a set of small, bounded diagnostic scratch files left in /tmp on both nodes (e.g. cmd-9d57be3301454c50, cmd-9608e792abd44c3a, cmd-b80e9b41433442e1, cmd-1b36ae9eda7c4318, cmd-88ba5f3c874c4ed2 wrote /tmp/out.txt, /tmp/src.txt, /tmp/cl*.txt, /tmp/pre_src*.txt, /tmp/post_src*.txt on node1 and node2), confirmed still present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot -- these were never cleaned up. The /etc/chrony.conf.bak backups created before editing (cmd-6d675b566a984865, cmd-37242a0f46df4592) are a reasonable, low-risk safety practice rather than unwanted residue. No failed/conflicting services, no destructive commands, and no weakened security controls were observed; the firewalld ntp exposure is a required consequence of the task itself.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9d57be3301454c50`, `cmd-9608e792abd44c3a`, `cmd-b80e9b41433442e1`, `cmd-1b36ae9eda7c4318`, `cmd-88ba5f3c874c4ed2`, `cmd-6d675b566a984865`, `cmd-37242a0f46df4592`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- No external clock-offset validation (e.g. comparing wall-clock drift) was captured, so synchronization accuracy beyond source selection cannot be independently confirmed.
- The prepare phase was disabled and after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare, so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor timeline rather than a distinct snapshot.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
